newsitem.title: UK: London gold drifts lower as bearish mood deepens.
newsitem.headline: London gold drifts lower as bearish mood deepens.

text.p: The price of gold edged down closer to a key support level on Tuesday in a market disappointed by the metal's failure to hang on to recent gains.
"It's drifting lower more on bearish sentiment than anything else," one London-based dealer said.

"A lot of gold has been sold in the last few days and dealers are more confident about playing the short side again." Bullion fixed at $378.30 an ounce, compared to $379.10 on Monday afternoon and a London close of $378.80/$379.30.
The bullish expectations of last week, on the back of a brisk rally to nearly $385 an ounce, were reversed after heavy selling from gold producers thwarted gold's rise, dealers said.
"There are more bears about now," one dealer noted. "This time of year you get sell-offs because the jewellery industry has done its business and business is very quiet."
A drop below $377, the 19-month low from which prices have bounced twice since early October, would point to more significant losses, dealers and analysts said.
"All big support lines get tested, and the feeling is it might dip below there," one dealer said.
The next nearby support level was around $374 an ounce.
Historical price charts showed the other precious metals also vulnerable to the downside, analysts said.
Silver was weaker at $4.87/$4.89 an ounce, down two cents from Monday's London close and off 10 cents from the highs of a rally late last Friday.
"On Friday silver shot up on shortcovering, which briefly stopped the selling in gold. But as soon as silver showed weakness, gold started being sold again," a dealer noted.
Technical analysts, referring to the futures contract on New York's Comex market, said the downside was favoured for silver.

"Silver's failure to hold above $394 is disappointing and has seen the technical indicators lose their upward momentum, as the metal remains hemmed within the $4.80-$4.94 range," analyst Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary. The platinum market was quiet but prices were sinking lower along with gold and silver, dealers said.
Platinum was indicated at $383.00/$384.00 an ounce, off $1.50 from Monday's London close. Despite finding support at this level, platinum had room to move to $380, dealers said.
Palladium was also easier at $117.75/$118.75, down $0.25.
